text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- Szczecin Shipyard President Krzysztof Piotrowski will meet the Gdansk shipyard receiver on Thursday to discuss the possiblity of financial engagement in the bankrupt Gdansk yard.
- Two Polish foreign traders operating on the Russian market, Bartimpex and Kolmex, accuse each other of unfair competition and have recently taken the matter to court.
- Over 50 firms from Poland and abroad are exhibiting their products at the Lodz-based "Yarn Market 96" organised by the Textilimpex foreign trade company.
- Poland's Industry Ministry and Britain's Know-How Fund have contracted Britain's Schroeders bank to assist the Polish power grid company (PSE) in its privatisation.
- Growing new motor car sales bode well for the listed motor industry companies such as Stomil and Debica tyre makers.

- Over 1,100 firms from 20 countries will participate in Poznan-based international fair events: the "Domexpo'96" consumer goods fair, the advertising products fair and the "Tour Salon'96" tourist firms fair.
- Nafta Polska Holding has demanded changes in the refineries privatisation programme so as to provide them with shares in CPN-owned petrol stations.
Nafta Polska officials said if their company was not granted stakes in the distribution network, foreign investors would most likely withdraw from refinery privatisation.
- Ruch, Poland's biggest press distribution network, has contracted computer paper delivery from the Kompap paper maker, which will increase the latter's sales revenue by 10 percent.
More than ninety banks, trust funds, insurance firms and brokerage houses will exhibit their offers at the second Polish capital investment forum to start in Warsaw tomorrow.
- The listed Rafako boiler maker's net profit in 1996's first eight months amounted to 10.6 million zlotys.
Company management is sticking with its forecast of a 1996 net profit of 23 million zlotys.
